# PGY1.com

> Disability insurance for resident and fellow physicians, explained by Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, an independent broker who has worked only with physicians for 25+ years and lectures at 100+ residency and fellowship programs a year.

PGY1 Financial Solutions Corp helps medical students, residents and fellows choose disability insurance at the start of training: GSI (guaranteed standard issue) policies with no health questions, own-occupation coverage, and what to do before Match Day and July 1. The answers on this site come from Jay's recorded webinars, in his own words, each with a short video clip.

Every page is available as markdown: add `.md` to the URL without the trailing slash (https://www.pgy1.com/questions/what-is-gsi-disability-insurance.md), or request any page with `Accept: text/markdown`.

Contact: (609) 432-8862 · jay@pgy1.com. General information, not advice for a specific situation.

## Start here

- [Disability Insurance for Resident and Fellow Physicians](https://www.pgy1.com/?utm_source=llms.txt): GSI policies with no health questions, true own-occupation coverage and an independent broker for residents and fellows. Start with a 2-minute form. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/index.md)
- [Disability insurance questions from residents and fellows](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/?utm_source=llms.txt): Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, answers the disability insurance questions residents, fellows and MS4s ask most, with clips from his webinars. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions.md)
- [Does your hospital have a GSI policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/gsi/?utm_source=llms.txt): Does your residency hospital offer a GSI disability policy with no health questions? Search the 29 teaching hospitals where Jay Weinberg offers one. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/gsi.md)
- [Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC](https://www.pgy1.com/about/?utm_source=llms.txt): Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, is an independent disability insurance broker who works only with physicians and lectures at 100+ residency programs a year. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/about.md)

(markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/disability-insurance-before-residency.md)
- [How much does disability insurance cost for a resident or fellow?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/disability-insurance-cost-resident/?utm_source=llms.txt): A budgeting rule of thumb from Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, for what disability insurance costs residents, fellows and graduating medical students. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/disability-insurance-cost-resident.md)
- [Is disability insurance more expensive in California?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/disability-insurance-california/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why California stands out for disability insurance pricing and wording, and what to consider if you're moving into or out of California for residency. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/disability-insurance-california.md)

## Questions: GSI policies

- [What is a GSI disability insurance policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/what-is-gsi-disability-insurance/?utm_source=llms.txt): What a GSI (guaranteed standard issue) disability policy is, how it differs from a medically underwritten one, and why residents should check for it first. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/what-is-gsi-disability-insurance.md)
- [Should I apply for a medically underwritten policy before checking for GSI?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/apply-underwritten-before-gsi/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why applying for a medically underwritten policy first can make you ineligible for GSI, and two questions to ask any insurance professional. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/apply-underwritten-before-gsi.md)
- [Can past mental health treatment affect getting disability insurance?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/mental-health-and-disability-insurance/?utm_source=llms.txt): How medical underwriting treats current or past mental health treatment for residents and fellows, and why a GSI policy may offer wider coverage. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/mental-health-and-disability-insurance.md)
- [What are the eligibility questions and limits of a GSI policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/gsi-eligibility-and-limitations/?utm_source=llms.txt): The Guardian GSI knockout questions, the main limitations of GSI disability policies, and why GSI offers may not stay available. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/gsi-eligibility-and-limitations.md)
- [I already applied for a medically underwritten policy. Can I still get GSI?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/already-applied-can-i-still-get-gsi/?utm_source=llms.txt): Applying for a medically underwritten disability policy usually rules out a GSI policy, but not always. Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, on the exceptions. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/already-applied-can-i-still-get-gsi.md)
- [Do GSI disability policies cost more?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/do-gsi-policies-cost-more/?utm_source=llms.txt): Do GSI disability policies cost residents more than medically underwritten ones? Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, explains why not for the Guardian GSI. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/do-gsi-policies-cost-more.md)
- [Why can't my GME office tell me if there's a GSI policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/why-gme-cant-tell-you-about-gsi/?utm_source=llms.txt): GSI policies usually aren't part of your hospital's benefits, so your GME office often can't tell you if one exists. How to find out instead. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/why-gme-cant-tell-you-about-gsi.md)
- [How do I tell a strong GSI policy from a scaled-back one?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/how-to-compare-gsi-policies/?utm_source=llms.txt): Not all GSI disability policies for residents are equal. The six things to check before you take one, from Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/how-to-compare-gsi-policies.md)
- [Can I wait until I finish training to get a GSI policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/wait-until-end-of-training-for-gsi/?utm_source=llms.txt): GSI offers can end at any time, usually without notice. Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, on why residents shouldn't wait until their last months of training. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/wait-until-end-of-training-for-gsi.md)
- [Does a GSI policy cover hobbies like scuba diving or rock climbing?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/gsi-hazardous-activities/?utm_source=llms.txt): GSI disability policies overlook pre-existing conditions and hobbies like scuba diving and rock climbing. Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, on who they suit. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/gsi-hazardous-activities.md)

## Questions: Choosing a policy

- [What is medical-specialty-specific true own-occupation disability insurance?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/own-occupation-disability-insurance/?utm_source=llms.txt): What own-occupation means in a physician disability policy, why medical specialty specific wording is strongest, and what "any gainful occupation" means. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/own-occupation-disability-insurance.md)
- [Is the group disability insurance from my employer enough?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/group-disability-insurance-enough/?utm_source=llms.txt): How employer group disability insurance compares with an individual policy for physicians: taxes, portability, contract language and benefit caps. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/group-disability-insurance-enough.md)
- [What is the future increase option on a disability policy?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/future-increase-option/?utm_source=llms.txt): What the future increase option (flex-up or balloon option) is on a physician disability policy, and why it matters most for residents and fellows. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/future-increase-option.md)
- [How do I choose a disability insurance agent?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/choosing-a-disability-insurance-agent/?utm_source=llms.txt): Red flags when an insurance professional shows you disability policies: one-page comparison grids, no pre-screening, too-good-to-be-true pricing. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/choosing-a-disability-insurance-agent.md)
- [How much disability coverage can I get as an attending?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/how-much-disability-coverage-attending/?utm_source=llms.txt): How much monthly disability coverage most physicians qualify for as attendings, and how GSI policy caps fit in, from Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/how-much-disability-coverage-attending.md)
- [What's the difference between short-term and long-term disability insurance?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/short-term-vs-long-term-disability/?utm_source=llms.txt): How short-term and long-term disability insurance differ in when they start paying and how long they pay, explained by Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/short-term-vs-long-term-disability.md)
- [What happens in medical underwriting, and can an exclusion be removed later?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/medical-underwriting-exclusions/?utm_source=llms.txt): What disability insurers look at in medical underwriting, the three possible outcomes, and how an exclusion can sometimes come off a policy later. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/medical-underwriting-exclusions.md)
- [Should I price shop disability insurance?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/price-shopping-disability-insurance/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why the cheapest physician disability policy is often missing key features, and what a too-good-to-be-true price usually means. Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/price-shopping-disability-insurance.md)
- [A friend or relative sells insurance. Should I use them for disability insurance?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/friend-or-family-who-sells-insurance/?utm_source=llms.txt): Most residents know someone who sells insurance. Why Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, says to pre-screen for a physician disability specialist instead. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/friend-or-family-who-sells-insurance.md)

## Questions: Medical school to residency

- [Disability insurance, student loans or a Roth IRA: what should I do first?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/what-to-prioritize-first/?utm_source=llms.txt): Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC, on the "pecking order" of a resident's financial plan, and why disability insurance and student loans usually come first. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/what-to-prioritize-first.md)
- [Should I file taxes as a fourth-year medical student with no income?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/file-taxes-as-ms4/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why fourth-year medical students should file a tax return even with no income, and how it can affect your PGY1 student loan payment. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/file-taxes-as-ms4.md)
- [Should I do a direct consolidation before residency?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/direct-consolidation-before-residency/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why a direct consolidation may not be the right move for medical students graduating in 2026, and how timing interacts with the new RAP repayment plan. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/direct-consolidation-before-residency.md)
- [IBR or RAP: which repayment plan should I pick as a resident?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/ibr-vs-rap-for-residents/?utm_source=llms.txt): How IBR and the new RAP student loan repayment plan compare for residents, and when each one may make more sense, from Jay Weinberg's March 2026 update. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/ibr-vs-rap-for-residents.md)
- [What do I need to qualify for Public Service Loan Forgiveness?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/pslf-requirements/?utm_source=llms.txt): The three requirements for Public Service Loan Forgiveness and why residents should certify employment every year, from Jay Weinberg, CLU, ChFC. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/pslf-requirements.md)
- [Should I refinance my student loans with a private lender as a resident?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/private-refinance-student-loans/?utm_source=llms.txt): When a private student loan refinance makes sense for residents, and why refinancing government loans gives up Public Service Loan Forgiveness. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/private-refinance-student-loans.md)
- [Should I rent or buy during residency?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/rent-or-buy-during-residency/?utm_source=llms.txt): How residents should think about renting vs buying, and how physician mortgages work, including lenders that accept a match letter. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/rent-or-buy-during-residency.md)
- [Should I open a Roth IRA as a resident?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/roth-ira-as-a-resident/?utm_source=llms.txt): Why a Roth IRA can make sense while you earn a resident's salary, how it works, and where it fits next to disability insurance. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/roth-ira-as-a-resident.md)
- [How should I budget and build an emergency fund in intern year?](https://www.pgy1.com/questions/budget-and-emergency-fund-intern-year/?utm_source=llms.txt): How to build your first budget on a resident's paycheck, how big an emergency fund should be, and what to take care of when you move for residency. (markdown: https://www.pgy1.com/questions/budget-and-emergency-fund-intern-year.md)
